purpose: This medication is used to help with fertility in both women and men. In women, it helps trigger the release of an egg from the ovary during fertility treatments. In men and boys, it can help treat certain hormonal conditions, including undescended testicles in young boys.
how_it_works: Chorionic gonadotropin is a hormone that acts a lot like a natural hormone your body already makes called LH (luteinizing hormone). In women, it sends a signal to the ovary saying it is time to release an egg, which is an important step when trying to get pregnant. In men, it signals the body to produce more testosterone and helps support sperm production.
common_side_effects: Headache, feeling tired, irritability, restlessness, mild swelling or pain at the injection site, bloating, and mood changes. Women may also experience pelvic discomfort or mild stomach pain.
warnings: There is a risk of a serious condition called Ovarian Hyperstimulation Syndrome (OHSS) in women, which can cause severe abdominal pain, swelling, and difficulty breathing — contact your doctor right away if this happens. This medication should not be used if you have certain hormone-sensitive cancers, uncontrolled thyroid or adrenal problems, or if you are already pregnant. Tell your doctor about all your medications and medical history before starting this drug.
typical_dosing: This medication is given as an injection, either under the skin or into a muscle, and is usually given by a healthcare provider or taught for home use. The dose and how often you use it depends on what it is being used for — your doctor will give you a very specific schedule tailored to your treatment plan. Never adjust your dose on your own without talking to your doctor first.
